name: clone
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::clone(Tensor self, *, MemoryFormat? memory_format=None) -> Tensor. This signature is representative only; it is not an exclusive contract. All registered signatures: aten::clone(Tensor self, *, MemoryFormat? memory_format=None) -> Tensor; aten::clone.out(Tensor self, *, MemoryFormat? memory_format=None, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). The original Gems pytest calls and results define the full contract that this definition must not narrow: overloading between the functional and out forms; the keyword-only memory_format argument, passed as torch.preserve_format, torch.contiguous_format, torch.channels_last or torch.channels_last_3d, or omitted so that the schema default (None) applies; a fresh copy whose storage is distinct from the input's (asserted only for non-empty inputs) and whose materialized lazy conjugate/negation flags match the native reference result's; strides and storage_offset compared row by row against the native reference for every layout row rather than hard-coded per format; the requirement that the input and any hidden parent padding are never written; the out overload returning its caller-provided buffer in place (res_out is buf, storage and storage_offset unchanged); backward producing a gradient that compares equal to the native reference gradient; and the error cases (non-tensor input, channels_last/channels_last_3d on the wrong rank, out dtype mismatch). Semantics from the tests: clone materializes a fresh copy of self that does not share storage with a non-empty input, leaves the input unmodified (the input is re-compared against a reference copy, and for lazy conjugate/negation inputs the result's is_conj()/is_neg() match the reference result's), and when out is given, copies into that tensor and returns it as an alias of out. The outputs/effects metadata describes the representative functional overload only; the out overload mutates its out argument, which the pytest covers.
